input_encoding: numeric case id = (10-Boolean mask << 2) | bufferPhase; Boolean bit i is inputs[i] for i < 10
limits: Exhaustive cases are synthetic abstract projections, not a claim that all vectors are reachable with two players and two cubes.

Synthetic contexts may exceed two body contacts or two cube entries and may combine runtime flags that sync would normalize. Every abstract input is nevertheless roundtripped through the actual current extractor/status projection.

Ordered fixtures use valid current records, exactly cubeA/cubeB and two body slots. They test reducers and snapshots, not geometry/reachability, WebSocket authorization, cube ownership or epoch acceptance.
Native code is stateless: it does not advance clocks, set latches, persist records, process arrivals, schedule crumble or authorize actions.
Raw signals, grace-inclusive physical power, current unlock candidate and existing durable exit door are separate outputs.
Crumble remains authored gameplay timing. Its warning/broken/stable observations are server evidence, never OLLVM/bogus-block evidence.
coordinator_scope: Accepted body contacts and cube semantic placements are fixture inputs, not a WebSocket reimplementation.
RACE buffer contact/reset seed the post-authorization runtime documented in server/multiplayer.ts:264-285; authority/epoch rejection is excluded.
coordinator-latch assigns the existing durable latch only after actual definition.unlock succeeds, matching server/multiplayer.ts:321-322. The prior candidate snapshot is intentionally pre-latch.
Restart serializes and validates the actual record with readRoomRecord, recreates fresh runtime and body contacts, and then uses the actual sync functions.

sequences.scope: Ordered actual exported server reducers and project/unlock; accepted semantic contacts/placements supplied by fixture, transport authorization/geometry excluded
